questions.q: As defined in the lesson, what is data provenance?
options: The documented history of where a piece of data originated and how it was collected
The file format a dataset is stored in
The total file size of a dataset
The name of the database server hosting the data
questions.explain: The lesson defines provenance as the documented history and origin of the data, not a technical storage detail.

questions.q: According to the lesson, how is consent different from legality?
options: Consent asks whether people actually agreed to this specific use, while legality only asks whether the use is permitted
Consent and legality mean exactly the same thing in every case
Consent only applies to data collected outside a person's home country
Legality is a stricter standard than consent in every situation
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes consent (specific agreement to this use) from legality (whether the use is technically permitted).

questions.q: Why does the lesson say public or scraped data has the murkiest provenance of the common sources discussed?
options: Because publicly visible is not the same as available for any use, and the people described were never asked anything
Because scraped data is always more accurate than internally collected data
Because scraped data cannot technically be stored in a database
Because public data is illegal to possess in any form
questions.explain: The lesson specifically notes that visibility does not equal permission, and scraped subjects were never asked for consent.

questions.q: What provenance question does licensed third-party data raise, per the lesson?
options: Whether the vendor's license to you extends to training a model, specifically
Whether the data was collected using a specific brand of computer
Whether the vendor's office is located domestically or internationally
Whether the data was collected before or after a holiday
questions.explain: The lesson highlights that a license permitting general use may not specifically cover training a model.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say 'we found it on the internet' is not an adequate provenance answer?
options: Because a governed organization needs to document the actual source, collection method, and consent or license basis before training
Because internet data is always technically corrupted
Because no data exists anywhere on the internet in practice
Because that phrase is grammatically incorrect
questions.explain: The lesson argues that phrase used to be treated as sufficient but doesn't meet the documentation bar a governed organization requires.
